room.name: Take the Shade With You
room.hint: Dash Down-Right, Strike, then Jump Left · Catch the lantern; carry its shade, then leave its weight on brass.
room.question: When does the thing you must carry become the thing you must leave behind?

bank.entrance: Small eastern launch perch beneath the phase cap.
bank.exit: Upper western chamber, above a pressure-held roof.
bank.author: Codex
bank.humanReview: User likes the design but found it too hard. Revised for a wider execution window; awaits another human review.
bank.solution: Dash down-right toward the outside tally, and cut during the dash. The dash raises the shade over the beam and makes the western shore solid. Once the tally lights, jump left: the late reversal grace lets this follow the cut as a readable sequence. The spent launch tongue still disappears behind you. Catch the suspended lantern on the return, carry its shade across the second beam, and land on the widened western shore. Drop the lantern on the extended brass strip to hold the roof open, then climb the west wall empty-handed.
bank.nearestExisting: F31 supplies the committed reverse launch. B34 uses a lantern catch to keep upward dash speed, while Return Freight recovers cargo from a moving deck. Here a horizontal reverse arc must acquire its shade in flight, then surrender that same cargo as a lasting roof weight.
bank.novelty: The outward/reverse commitment is now physical: a dash-operated shade permits the cut, and the spent footing removes the second launch setup. The return must then collect portable shade, cross a second beam, and turn that cargo into stationary weight so the knight can climb empty-handed.
bank.designNotes: Second human review found the idea good but the action nearly impossible. The survive-2 profile now remembers a grounded dash for an eight-frame post-dash reverse-jump grace; stale outgoing wall momentum cannot overwrite the reversal. A ground-skimming dash also accepts a later Strike, removing the exact simultaneous button chord. Forward hyper speed, dash refill rules and unprofiled rooms are unchanged. Receiving shore extends four tiles and the brass deposit strip extends four tiles, preventing a valid later launch from arriving just below the floor edge. All fourteen consecutive reversal delays 7–20 complete, and five offset Strike presses complete. Departure beam, remote tally and spent perch still physically enforce the outward commitment.

bank.hintTeaching: Strike can now follow the ground dash instead of sharing its exact frame. Once the right tally lights, hold Left and press Jump; a short grace accepts the reversal even just after the dash ends. Press Grab near the hanging lantern; the wider receiving floor and brass strip make the handoff unhurried.
